title: LLM Content Exposure Assessment
subtitle: Unified client assessment across Exposure Mapping and Forensic Depth Similarity Mapping
narrative: Across two testing drives, this assessment evaluated 4 model(s) over 400 prompt(s) and 2000 recorded execution(s). Drive 1 (Exposure Mapping) covered 350 single-execution probes with an overall observed exposure rate of 55.4%. Drive 2 (Forensic Depth Similarity) covered 50 prompts executed three times each, with average similarity 41.0 and average consistency 96.8. Within the tested scope, Gemini demonstrated the highest observed exposure indicators, while Claude demonstrated the lowest. In total, 483 high-severity risk label(s) were assigned by the judge across both drives. Figures below are observational and limited to the evaluated prompt set.

keyFindings.title: Gemini showed the highest observed exposure within scope
keyFindings.body: Across available drives, Gemini ranked highest on combined exposure indicators (Drive 1 exposure rate 82.9%, Drive 2 exposure rate 40.0%).

keyFindings.title: Repeated-run behaviour was not uniformly stable
keyFindings.body: Gemini produced 5 inconsistent prompt outcome(s) across three independent runs — pass/fail changed between attempts for those prompts.

keyFindings.title: Forensic similarity identified high-score matches
keyFindings.body: 64 prompt/model case(s) scored ≥ 70 on the forensic similarity scale, indicating stronger reconstruction of proprietary reference material within the tested scope.

keyFindings.title: Exposure Mapping separated models clearly
keyFindings.body: In Drive 1, Gemini showed an exposure rate of 82.9% across 350 prompts, versus Claude at 26.0%.

conclusions: Two complementary drives were executed: Exposure Mapping (elicitation) and Forensic Depth Similarity (reconstruction quality).
Repeated-run analysis found 19 inconsistent prompt/model case(s), which should be reviewed separately from fully stable outcomes.
483 high-severity judge risk label(s) warrant prioritized review.
Conclusions are scoped to the evaluated prompts and should not be generalised beyond this assessment set.

comparison.lede: Exposure Mapping identifies whether proprietary knowledge can be elicited. Forensic Similarity Mapping then measures the depth and nature of that reconstruction.
methodFlow: Exposure Mapping — detects elicitable proprietary familiarity (Drive 1, 350 prompts, one run).
Forensic Similarity Mapping — measures reconstruction depth, indicators, and three-run reliability (Drive 2, 50 prompts × 3).
comparison.howToRead: A model may show high elicitation exposure in Drive 1 and still vary in forensic similarity depth in Drive 2. Use Drive 1 for breadth of exposure risk and Drive 2 for strength/consistency of reconstruction.

rows.drive2: 3 independent runs per prompt per model

drive1Purpose: Assess whether tested models demonstrate knowledge of proprietary book content when probed with purpose-built exposure prompts. Each prompt was executed once per model.
drive2Purpose: Measure the degree and nature of similarity between model responses and proprietary reference material. Each prompt was executed three independent times per model to assess regeneration consistency.
